verdict: Duolingo grew daily users 29% and revenue 14% to $309M, but heavier research spending and stock pay trimmed net income to $27M — and a year ago the bottom line was flattered by a one-time $223M tax benefit.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $309M, vs $272M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $5.95 a year ago — that quarter included a one-time $223M tax benefit

kpis.label: Daily active users
kpis.note: Up 29% YoY — growth accelerated for a second straight quarter

segments.name: Subscriptions
segments.note: Paid plans (Super, and the Max tier being wound down) — by far the biggest money-maker. Up 18% as paid subscribers reached 13.1M.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown to free users. Roughly flat, down 1%.

segments.name: Duolingo English Test
segments.note: The company's online English proficiency exam, accepted by universities. Up 2%.

segments.name: In-app purchases
segments.note: One-off purchases inside the app, like gems and boosts. Down 38%.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Everything else. Small, but more than tripled.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the app and its AI features — the biggest running cost, up 30% YoY, including $32M of stock pay.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. Up 16% YoY.

otherDetail: Interest income of $12.4M on the cash pile, less $1.1M of other expense, net.
follow100Note: The rows above Kept as profit add to $100; Kept as profit is what was left of each $100 after all costs, other income and tax.

takeaways.title: Users are growing faster again
takeaways.text: Daily active users rose 29% to 64.9M — a second straight quarter of faster growth — helped by hundreds of small product experiments and game partnerships (Brawl Stars, Eggy Party) that brought in millions of learners. Monthly users reached 153.1M, up 13%.

takeaways.title: Subscriptions do the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 14% to $309M. Subscriptions were $270M of it, up 18%, while advertising was flat and in-app purchases fell 38%. Bookings — cash committed by customers — rose 12% to $316M, and paid subscribers hit 13.1M.

takeaways.title: Profit shrank as spending rose
takeaways.text: Net income fell to $27M from $292M a year ago — but that year-ago figure included a one-time $223M tax benefit. The real story is cost: operating expenses rose 24% to $201M, including $49M of stock pay, so operating profit fell to $24M. The company's Adjusted EBITDA was $79M, a 25.5% margin.

oneTimers: The year-ago quarter (Q3 2025) included a one-time $222.7M income-tax benefit from releasing a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets — that is why net income then was $292M and EPS was $5.95. This quarter's $27M profit has no such boost.

Research and development includes a $1.6M impairment of capitalized software, and stock-based compensation across the company was $49M in the quarter — a real cost to shareholders even though no cash left the building.
